source.title: Deep Double Descent: Where Bigger Models and More Data Hurt
source.authors: Preetum Nakkiran; Gal Kaplun; Yamini Bansal; Tristan Yang; B. Barak; I. Sutskever

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper trains neural networks from initialization across model sizes and training durations, and reports training error on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, including settings with label noise.
record.gate_note: Training-error curves bear on V1. The paper also reports test-error results, but those do not measure the training-error behavior in the claim versions. No results test V2–V6.
record.test_reason: The study reports training classification error for randomly initialized CNNs and ResNets on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 across widths, training durations, optimizers and label-noise conditions, directly testing V1.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate but understates the main conclusion: the authors propose effective model complexity to unify model-wise and epoch-wise double descent, and show settings where more training data worsens test performance. Near-zero training error defines interpolation in this account; the paper also explicitly distinguishes models too small to interpolate.
record.recipe_differences: Uses cross-entropy training on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 with CNNs and ResNets, varying model size and training duration; includes noisy-label settings. The paper does not test every recipe or comparison in V1.
record.method_sensitivity: Training duration and model size; the paper also varies label noise, dataset, optimizer, and data augmentation across experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Test error can exhibit double descent as model width or training duration increases, and additional training samples can sometimes worsen test performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generalization can vary non-monotonically with model size, training duration, and sample count near the interpolation threshold.

record.problems: Training-error values relevant to V1 are shown in figures rather than reported numerically in the text. The experiments use some label-noise levels, not fully random labels.

untested.parts: Fully random labels are not experimentally tested here; the introductory statement about fitting them cites prior work. The experiments do not establish the claim for every sufficiently large architecture or training recipe.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student optimization, spurious-minimum frequencies, and one- or two-neuron student overparameterization.
Depth-dependent training degradation and comparisons with identity shortcuts, special tanh initialization, or Fixup.
Comparisons of initialization schemes, signal or gradient propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to initial stability thresholds, curvature dynamics, catapult recovery, and edge-of-stability behavior.
Training-speed and learning-rate comparisons with versus without batch normalization, including Fixup.

missing.what: Training-error results comparing SGD and Adam directly; the record incorrectly treats this comparison as untested. Extract readable outcomes by optimizer and width.
Training-error results with and without data augmentation, which shifts the interpolation threshold.

The explicit distinction between models too small to interpolate, medium models that barely reach approximately zero training error, and larger models that interpolate during training. Record separate size and duration conditions.
Training-error trajectories for fixed-width ResNets on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, complementing the CNN trajectory already recorded.

Training-error comparisons across weight-decay conditions for CNNs on CIFAR-10 with 10% label noise. These directly address the regularized-recipe component; Figure 22 separately reports training loss, which should not be substituted for classification error.
Additional clean CIFAR-100 and noisy CIFAR-10 training-performance maps across model sizes and epochs, relevant to interpolation and early stopping.

record.verdict_notes: This study is an original source for V1, so no verdict labels are assigned. Figure-only rows remain linked to V1, but their condition-specific states cannot be verified from the supplied text. Qualitative statements establish that the study tests V1 without supplying the missing curve values.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 training error with some label noise, but not fully random labels, Adam versus SGD as a direct comparison of training-error outcomes, or early stopping and smaller-model effects as a comprehensive comparison.

relation.reason: Its own training-error results and discussion of interpolation directly bear on V1.

tranche.reason: This V1 original source directly measures training classification error in CNNs and ResNets on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 using SGD or Adam across model sizes, training durations, and noise conditions.

source_check.notes: Numerical training-error values are unavailable in the extracted figures, so cannot_determine is appropriate for these rows. The introduction's random-label fitting statement cites Zhang et al.; it is not this study's own fully random-label experiment.

statements.correction: R1–R2: CIFAR-10, 15% label noise, Adam. R3: CIFAR-100, varying label noise including none, Adam. Section 4: corrupted labels sampled once, retained across epochs. No reported fully randomized-label Adam experiment; no explicit exclusion statement.
statements.problem: The characterization of the reported Adam settings is supported, but the paper does not explicitly exclude fully randomized labels; it does not report that experiment.
